evidence: src/domain/order.ts: advanceTo() uses nextState(this.currentState) and cancel() uses isCancellable(this.currentState) from src/domain/order-state.ts. The transition rules live only in order-state.ts.
src/domain/order-state.ts: FULFILMENT_FLOW and CANCELLABLE are the only definitions of the order lifecycle, and assertOrderState reuses isOrderState.

src/domain/stock-reservation.ts: reserveStock checks with product.canReserve(quantity) and changes stock only through productFor(...).reserve(quantity). It never touches Product's private reserved or onHand fields.

src/domain/stock-reservation.ts and src/domain/product.ts: both throw DomainError("insufficient_stock", `Insufficient stock for product ...: requested ..., available ...`). The message is repeated, but the check itself stays in Product.canReserve.
src/domain/domain-error.ts: DomainError and DomainErrorCode are the single error type used by order-line.ts, order-state.ts, order.ts, product.ts and stock-reservation.ts.
src/domain/order-repository.ts and src/domain/product-repository.ts: these port interfaces deal only in the module's own Order, OrderState and Product types.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module covers one concern: ordering with stock reservation. That concern is built from a few parts: entities (Order, OrderLine, Product), the order lifecycle rules (order-state.ts), stock reservation across order lines (stock-reservation.ts), repository ports and one shared error type. Each file uses the module's own building blocks. Every file raises errors as DomainError with a code from DomainErrorCode. Order.advanceTo uses nextState() and Order.cancel uses isCancellable() rather than keeping its own copy of the transition rules. isOrderState and assertOrderState both build on FULFILMENT_FLOW. reserveStock checks stock through Product.canReserve and changes stock only through Product.reserve, so the rule 'quantity <= available' lives only in Product. One smaller issue: reserveStock builds its own 'insufficient_stock' DomainError with the same message text as Product.reserve. Its pre-check is needed so that either every line is reserved or none is. It reuses canReserve rather than restating the rule, so this is a repeated message, not a repeated rule. A small inconsistency is that reserveStock fails with not_found for a missing product, while releaseStock silently skips it. Together these fall short of the Fail criteria: no unrelated concerns, no duplicated rule, no bypassed abstraction.
